pages.text: "Yummy bread!" Bami hurried into the dining car, feet black from playing on coal sacks in the freight car. Mom set down steaming bread. Bami grabbed it with sooty feet. "Your feet?" Mom asked. Bami pretended not to hear.
"Washing takes too long! I'll eat and go back to the coal sacks!" Bami gobbled. Tiny smiling wrigglers hopped from their black toes onto the bread. Bami didn't notice.
Soon their tummy rumbled and ached. "Oh, my tummy..." Bami curled by the window, eyes watering. Pipi called from the roof, "A station!"
The train stopped. A mole postman with a mailbag entered the dining car. "Coal-dust wrigglers rode your bread into your tummy!" he said, seeing Bami's feet. "Come to the washroom with me."
They stood together, one pair of clean feet beside one black pair. "I dig all day, so I'm an expert foot-washer. Three steps! One, get them wet!" He turned on the water, and Bami followed.
"Two, make soapy bubbles!" He rubbed his feet until white foam rose. "Like clouds!" Bami rubbed both feet happily. The postman sang, "Wash your feet, then eat!"
"Three, scrub and rinse between your toes!" Bami rubbed and rinsed the wriggling germs away. "One, two, three—squeaky clean! Bye, germs!" Together they sang, "Wash your feet, then eat!"
Patting their feet dry left them clean and soft. After a good rest, Bami's tummy gradually felt better. "Washing before eating will keep my tummy happy!" Bami spread their wings and hopped.
Next day, spring rain fell outside at snack time. "Wait! Feet first!" Bami called. "One, wet! Two, bubbles! Three, scrub and rinse between the toes!" Now Bami could do it alone.
Mom cuddled clean-footed Bami. "Our foot-washing champion!" Washing before eating kept their tummy happy and left them refreshed. Wash your feet, then eat! Today's bread tasted twice as good.
